system_note: Reviewed billed revenue line: Rev Code 0192 (Rehabilitation therapy), 10 units billed for 01/08/2026-01/21/2026. The medical record shows a PT evaluation/certification and an interdisciplinary plan calling for PT/OT 5-7x/week, documented therapy sessions on the 10 billed dates, and explicit facility-level notes that weekend dates had no therapy and were billed Level 1 (Rev 0191). Evidence: the PT Evaluation/Plan documents a certification period and plan of treatment (Physical Therapy, Physical Therapy, p. 18-20) and the Interdisciplinary Plan of Care specifies "- Skilled PT evaluation and treatment 5-7x/week per plan of care" (INTERDISCIPLINARY PLAN OF CARE - SNF STAY, p. 10-11). The Treatment Administration Record documents completed therapy on the first therapy date (TREATMENT ADMINISTRATION RECORD | 01/08/2026, p. 139: "PT session 60 min completed per therapy schedule; nurse facilitated patient preparation; positioning maintained post-treatment"), and the facility explicitly documents that weekend days had no therapy and were Level 1 per-diem (SKILLED NURSING PROGRESS NOTE | 01/10/2026, p. 86-87: "No therapy scheduled today (weekend/non-therapy day). Skilled nursing care provided per orders. Level 1 per diem billing (Rev 0191)."; SKILLED NURSING PROGRESS NOTE | 01/17/2026, p. 100-101: same). The claim billed 10 days of Rev 0192 which matches the documented therapy dates (01/08, 01/09, 01/12-01/16, 01/19-01/21) in the therapy/daily-services extract. The dataset lacks a payer-specific numeric minute threshold for 0192 (fallback reference guide has no minute thresholds), so the audit relies on the facility's therapy plan, certification, and documented sessions. Conclusion: documentation supports the 10 billed 0192 per-diem days as submitted; no adjustment required. Reviewed revenue line: billed revenue code 0191 (Skilled Nursing) for dates 2026-01-08 through 2026-01-21 (claim MR_SNF_07). Claim header documents the skilled care basis as: "Skilled nursing for cardiac monitoring, diuretic titration, and daily weight monitoring with PT/OT reconditioning following acute decompensation of systolic CHF" (Claim MR_SNF_07, claim row). Therapy treatment records show PT/OT sessions with 60 min PT + 45 min OT on multiple dates (e.g. 2026-01-08, 2026-01-09, 2026-01-12, 2026-01-13, 2026-01-14, 2026-01-15, 2026-01-16, 2026-01-19, 2026-01-20, 2026-01-21) (get_daily_services output). The dataset contains no payer-specific per-diem numeric thresholds (fallback to payer-agnostic reference guide), which only defines revenue code meanings and states the MDS "supports but does not replace" daily clinical documentation (Policy Documents/SNF/...SNF Level of Care - Definitions and Reference Guide.docx, positions 8 and 9). The per-diem-level extraction tool returned NULL level_determination_statement for every date in the range; the tool's metadata notes that a NULL means the facility did not document an explicit per-diem exception and that NULL alone "does NOT by itself mean the day is unsupported" (get_per_diem_level_notes output). However, several dates in the billed range have no therapy session rows in the daily services extract (notably 2026-01-10, 2026-01-11, 2026-01-17, 2026-01-18) and no nursing-specific progress notes were retrieved to document the daily skilled nursing interventions referenced in the claim header. Because the reviewer cannot confirm from the retrieved record that licensed skilled nursing services were documented on every billed date in the 01/08-01/21 range (the audit requires day-by-day support), and the dataset lacks payer-specific per-diem criteria and any nursing note evidence for the gap dates, there is insufficient evidence to determine that the billed 0191 level is fully supported for the entire date range. Recommendation: obtain the missing daily nursing notes/MDS entries or payer guideline numeric criteria to validate each billed date before issuing a per-diem downcoding or day-adjustment finding.

level_determination_statement is null on a date when the daily note doesn't state an explicit per-diem-level exception for it - that does NOT by itself mean the day is unsupported; it commonly means the billed level's own minute threshold was met that day, so the facility had no exception to document. A non-null statement is the facility's own basis for downcoding that specific date.
